reason: Top-k selection on disconnected training graphs can cut the repeated stationary eigenspace. This alternative changes the signal objective instead of claiming to repair the existing eigensolver.
definition: Y = ((I + A_hat)/2)^t (I-S) Z, where S projects onto all component stationary modes and independent Z_ij have distribution N(0,1/r).
score: One half of the squared difference between endpoint signal rows. Its expectation is the corresponding full-kernel squared row distance divided by two. Relative variance is 2/r for a nonzero target score.
execution_scope: Component labels are computed on CPU. Stationary projection, sparse filtering, predictor inference, and gradients run on CUDA. Gaussian probes use a local CPU generator and are copied to CUDA without changing the global RNG.
protocol: Same saved clean checkpoints, training graphs, ordered validation queries, edge budgets, and per-step proposal caps as the referenced eigen-signal runs. Each new run also includes ungrouped search controls. No test queries were evaluated.
source_hashes: Every source SHA recorded at run start was checked against the unchanged local source after both runs completed.

tests.command: OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 MKL_NUM_THREADS=4 python -m unittest discover -s tests

mathematical_checks: CPU and CUDA sparse filtering match a small double-precision dense full-kernel oracle.
All stationary components are removed even when component count exceeds sketch width.
Weighted duplicate edges, explicit loops, zero-weight bridges, isolated nodes, and negative nonstationary eigenvalues are covered.
Fixed-probe permutation equivariance and seeded sketch reproducibility are checked.
A wide sketch approximates exact full-kernel scores; finite-width sketches are not exact spectral embeddings.
interpretation: No consistent independent explanation benefit from diffusion grouping in this pilot. Neutral and adverse cases are retained. Resolving a signal-definition problem is not evidence of superior fidelity.
limits: Only two graphs, one training seed each, one sketch seed, and twenty previously used validation queries per graph.
Matching per-step proposal caps does not match actual evaluated proposals or total runtime.
Recorded offline times are not a controlled speedup comparison and do not measure whole-pipeline scalability.
Random or structural grouping controls and sketch-seed stability remain to be evaluated.
The prior eigen branch remains unchanged by default, including its known cutoff ambiguity.
No numerical manuscript results were changed.
